newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: INTERVIEW-Argentine CAPSA to expand aggressively.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Argentine CAPSA to expand aggressively.

text.p: The sale of a stake in Argentine energy firm CAPSA to El Paso Energy Corp last month was a strategic move to help CAPSA expand in Latin America, a top company official said Friday.
"The sale was done on CAPSA's initiative," Claudio Armada, head of CAPSA's investors relations, told Reuters. "The company chose a strategic partner with really aggressive expansion plans."
"El Paso will provide projects under study or already under development not only in Argentina, but also in Brazil, Chile and Bolivia," Armada said.
In Chile and Bolivia, they will transport gas while in Brazil they will also generate electricity, Armada said.
Separately, CAPSA and CAPEX qualified in March to take part in Venezuela's oil privatization drive.
Armada said El Paso will back capacity expansion plans.
El Paso's unit El Paso Energy International Co paid $157 million for a 29 percent stake in CAPSA, and terms include options to increase it up to 45 percent.
The remaining 71 percent of CAPSA is owned by the Argentine Gotz family.
CAPSA's owns 100 percent of the Diadema oil field and 55 percent of CAPEX SA, a generator with a 382-megawatt (MW) gas-fired power plant, both in southern Neuquen province.
Armada said El Paso would help expand business at both CAPSA and CAPEX, which together form an integrated energy company.

A $140 million 240 MW combined cycle expansion is under development at the Agua del Cajn plant, to be completed by May 1999, Armada said. This plant, operational since 1995, uses gas from CAPEX's Neuqun field.
CAPEX, which has a four percent share of the very dispersed Argentine electric market, also owns 24 percent of the 76 MW Energa del Sur gas-fired power plant.
Armada said the merger also spelled benefits for El Paso.
"CAPEX may serve as a foothold for El Paso in Latin America."
CAPEX is also in the preliminary stages of filing to list on Nasdaq in the near future, Armada said.
"After the merger, we are even more resolved to do so."
In fiscal 1995-96, CAPEX posted a $28 million profit.

Armada said the company is building a $20-$25 million plant to process an additional two million cubic meters of gas a day which, according to market sources, would add some $5 million of profit in fiscal 1998/99. CAPEX now produces 2.5 million cubic meters of gas a day.
